subject: physical-education
title: Physical Fitness and Disease Prevention
summary: This chapter explores the components of physical fitness, the relationship between lifestyle choices and non-communicable diseases, the dangers of substance abuse, and fundamental principles of exercise physiology.

sections.title: Components of Physical Fitness
sections.content: Physical fitness is the ability to perform daily activities with vigor without undue fatigue. It comprises five health-related components: cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength, muscular endurance, flexibility, and body composition. Cardiovascular endurance refers to the heart and lungs' ability to supply oxygen during sustained activity, while muscular strength is the maximum force a muscle can generate in a single effort. Muscular endurance allows muscles to perform repeated contractions over time, and flexibility is the range of motion around joints. Skill-related components such as agility, balance, coordination, power, reaction time, and speed are also important for athletic performance.

sections.title: Lifestyle Diseases: Diabetes and Heart Disease
sections.content: Lifestyle diseases are non-communicable conditions linked to daily habits such as poor diet, physical inactivity, smoking, and excessive alcohol consumption. Type 2 diabetes occurs when the body becomes resistant to insulin or fails to produce enough, leading to high blood sugar levels that damage organs over time. Cardiovascular diseases including hypertension, heart attack, and stroke are major causes of death in Bangladesh and worldwide. Regular aerobic exercise, a diet low in saturated fats and refined sugars, maintaining healthy body weight, and avoiding tobacco use are key preventive measures. Early detection through regular health check-ups can significantly reduce complications and improve quality of life.

sections.title: Drug Awareness and Substance Abuse
sections.content: Drug abuse refers to the harmful use of legal or illegal substances including tobacco, alcohol, cannabis, yaba (methamphetamine), heroin, and prescription medications. Substance abuse leads to physical dependence, mental health disorders, financial ruin, and social breakdown within families and communities. In Bangladesh, yaba addiction has become a serious concern among youth, contributing to crime and health crises. Prevention strategies include education about the dangers of drugs, building strong family relationships, engaging in sports and creative activities, and developing refusal skills. Treatment options such as counseling, rehabilitation centers, and government awareness campaigns help individuals recover and reintegrate into society.

sections.title: Exercise Physiology Basics
sections.content: Exercise physiology studies how the body responds and adapts to physical activity. During exercise, the cardiovascular system increases heart rate and blood flow to deliver oxygen to working muscles, while the respiratory system increases breathing rate to facilitate gas exchange. Muscles use adenosine triphosphate (ATP) for contraction, derived from aerobic (with oxygen) and anaerobic (without oxygen) energy systems. Regular training produces adaptations including increased stroke volume, improved lung capacity, stronger bones, and enhanced metabolic efficiency. The FITT principle — Frequency, Intensity, Time, and Type — guides the design of effective exercise programs tailored to individual fitness goals and health conditions.
